observations.seen: No directional flood key is readable. The infield and grass are lit almost evenly, with only a faint warm hotspot near the mound in Harbor. The Lunar frame is uniformly dim gray-beige with no light pools from the visible stadium lights.
Players have only faint, soft contact smudges at their feet. The mound has a slight darker rim, but no player, bat or wall casts a directional shadow.
Every surface reads fully matte: white uniforms, bases, helmets and the scoreboard glass show no specular highlights or environment reflection.

Each arena has a theme (harbor stands, giant canyon boulders, lunar night, a midtown skyline). The props are crude, though. The canyon boulders sit at odd scale behind the wall, and the skyline buildings use smeared, stretched textures with flat cyan billboard rectangles.
There is no indoor haze, depth fog or light shafts. The canyon sky is a flat gray band, and the lunar sky is black with point dots.

Infield dirt uses a large blotchy noise pattern that reads as camouflage, most visibly as pink mottling in Midtown. The grass is flat color with faint mow stripes, and the uniforms are untextured white.
Players are low-poly figures with simple caps and gloves. Bases are plain slabs. The infield is a lumpy cloverleaf shape rather than a regulation diamond cut.
The infield dirt fills roughly 60% of the frame, above the 25–40% target. The horizon and stands are squeezed into the top band, and in Harbor the scoreboard HUD covers the left stands.
All four frames use the same fixed high perspective behind home plate. It reads clearly but is not the orthographic broadcast view the recipe asks for, and the outfielders shrink to a few pixels.
No bloom, grading or vignette is evident beyond a slight warm cast in Harbor. Lunar looks crushed and desaturated rather than graded.
The line score, count, outs, bases and matchup panels are tidy. The inning header numerals are low contrast, the HTML nav bar along the top dominates, and the controls strip reads as debug text.
